title: Autonomous Workflow Orchestration
breadcrumb: Services > Agentic AI & Hyperautomation > Autonomous Workflow Orchestration
meta_description: Autonomous Workflow Orchestration from Dataq Software: scope, delivery pattern, platforms and committed outcomes.

blocks.x: Most autonomous workflow orchestration engagements stall between the deck and the deployment. Ours are built to cross that gap: Self-healing workflows — long-running business processes that adapt, retry and recover without tickets.. What follows is the working pattern, not the brochure.
What we deliver under this name

Enterprise workflows fail silently: a settlement instruction missing a reference, an order blocked on inventory that never arrived, an onboarding task stalled for two weeks. We build orchestration that watches itself — durable execution with saga patterns, automatic compensation on failure, timeout-aware escalation, and agentic remediation that resolves the recoverable 80% (reformat a file, re-request a document, reroute an approval) before a human ever sees a ticket.

Every workflow is versioned, simulated against historical traces before deployment, and monitored with SLOs per business outcome — not per microservice. The result is operational: order-to-cash, onboarding, claims and reconciliation flows that complete at higher rates with fewer touches, and an operations team that manages exceptions by policy instead of by inbox.

Programs of Autonomous Workflow Orchestration run in Logistics & Supply Chain, Banking & Financial Services, Insurance & Risk, Manufacturing & Industrial — always against one named number, always with the baseline signed first.
What ships, in the order it ships:

items: Durable execution core
saga-pattern workflows with compensation and idempotency
Agentic remediation
recovery playbooks executed by agents for the recoverable failure classes
Simulation gate
new workflow versions replayed against historical traces pre-deploy
Outcome SLOs
business-level service objectives (completion rate, cycle time) with alerting
Escalation design
policy-routed human queues with full context handoff
